title: The hanifs
hookLine: a few people refused the idols and sought the religion of Ibrahim

lines: A MAN, HIS BACK TO THE KA'BA.
cards: A man stands with his back pressed against the wall of the Ka'ba, facing the crowd instead of the idols. Asma, the daughter of Abu Bakr, remembered him there, and Sahih al-Bukhari keeps her memory.
He is calling out to the people of Quraysh: none of you follows the religion of Ibrahim except me. His name is Zayd ibn Amr. No book of his own, no community behind him.
Just a wall at his back and a refusal. Today's word is what people called someone like him.

teach.h: HANIF: TURNED TOWARD THE ONE GOD.
teach.b: The word is hanif. Pickthall renders it upright; others explain it as one who turns from false worship toward the one God. The Qur'an uses it more than once for Ibrahim.

teach.h: THE RELIGION OF ABRAHAM, THE UPRIGHT.
teach.b: In surah three, Pickthall translates: "So follow the religion of Abraham, the upright. He was not of the idolaters." In surah sixteen, Ibrahim is "by nature upright." Hanif is the word under both.

So in a Mecca crowded with idols, tradition remembers a few people who looked at all of it and said no. No scripture, no congregation. Just a name, Ibrahim, and a conviction that the House belonged to one God.
Zayd ibn Amr is one of them remembered by name in al-Bukhari, and the reports about him are concrete.

teach.h: NO MEAT FOR IDOLS. DON'T KILL HER.
teach.b: He would not eat meat sacrificed to idols.
His reason, as al-Bukhari gives it: God created the sheep, sent down the rain, and grew the grass, and still people slaughtered it in names other than His.
Asma remembers, too, that when a father meant to kill his little daughter, Zayd would step in. Don't kill her, he would say. I'll feed her for you.
Another report says he traveled north asking learned people about true religion, was pointed back to the religion of Ibrahim, and lifted his hands and declared that he was on it.
The sirah says he died before the revelation began. So a hanif wasn't a member of a movement with a meeting place.
Some readers describe the word as a direction rather than a club: someone already turned toward God, before there was a road to walk on.

how: The Qur'an calls its listeners to follow the religion of Ibrahim, the upright (3:95), and its verses calling Ibrahim hanif are recited in classes and sermons on pure worship of the one God.

o: upright: one turned from idols toward the one God
a hermit who left Mecca to live in a cave
a pilgrim who walked around the Ka'ba each year

p: upright, turned toward the one God
the religion of Abraham, the upright

s: the hanifs were an organized sect with a meeting place
the word describes a direction: someone turned toward the one God, often alone.
the Qur'an calls Ibrahim a hanif
Zayd ibn Amr refused meat sacrificed to idols
al-Bukhari reports it, with his reason: God made the sheep, the rain and the grass.

games.q: you're Zayd ibn Amr in a Mecca full of idols. you've turned away from them, but you have no scripture and no community. what do you do?
o: give up and rejoin the crowd.
travel, asking learned people about the religion of Ibrahim.
carve a new god of your own.
games.why: a report says he traveled north asking, was pointed back to the religion of Ibrahim, and declared he was on it.

practice: Find one thing you hold to quietly, even when the room around you doesn't: that people deserve dignity, that a promise is a promise, that God is one, whatever is truly yours.

Don't argue for it; just hold it, steady, not loud, the way Zayd leaned his back against that wall. If you pray, you can ask Allah to keep you firm on it; if you don't, simply notice what it's like to stand on something.

wordCard.voice: Hanif. Upright: one who turns from false worship toward the one God. The Qur'an's word for Ibrahim. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: a few kept looking. Tomorrow, Zamzam found again. See you there.
